Horizontal marking.title: Solid line
Horizontal marking.description:
Separates opposing traffic flows and marks lane boundaries at dangerous locations on roads; marks the boundaries of vehicle parking spaces.

Crossing lines 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3 is prohibited.

Horizontal marking.title: Edge of the carriageway
Horizontal marking.description:
Marks the edge of the carriageway or the boundaries of areas of the carriageway into which entry is prohibited.

Crossing lines 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3 is prohibited.

Line 1.2 may be crossed to stop on the shoulder and to re-enter the carriageway where stopping or parking is permitted.

Horizontal marking.title: Double solid line
Horizontal marking.description:
Separates opposing traffic flows on roads with four or more lanes in both directions, and on roads with two or three lanes where the lane width exceeds 3.75 m.

Crossing lines 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3 is prohibited.

Horizontal marking.title: No stopping
Horizontal marking.description: Marks places where stopping is prohibited.

Horizontal marking.title: Broken line
Horizontal marking.description:
Separates opposing traffic flows on roads with two or three lanes; marks lane boundaries where two or more lanes are provided for traffic in the same direction.

Lines 1.5–1.8 may be crossed from either side.

Horizontal marking.title: Approach line
Horizontal marking.description:
Warns of an approach to marking 1.1 or 1.11 separating traffic flows in opposite or the same directions.

Lines 1.5–1.8 may be crossed from either side.

Horizontal marking.title: Junction lanes and parking area
Horizontal marking.description:
Marks traffic lanes within a junction or a parking area. Blue markings indicate that the parking area is subject to payment.

Lines 1.5–1.8 may be crossed from either side.

Horizontal marking.title: Acceleration or deceleration lane boundary
Horizontal marking.description:
Marks the boundary between an acceleration or deceleration lane and the main carriageway lane.

Lines 1.5–1.8 may be crossed from either side.

Horizontal marking.title: Reversible lane
Horizontal marking.description:
Marks the boundaries of lanes with reversible traffic control; separates opposing traffic flows, when reversible traffic signals are switched off, on roads with reversible traffic control.

When reversible traffic signals are absent or switched off, line 1.9 may be crossed if it is on the driver’s right. When reversible traffic signals are operating, it may be crossed from either side if it separates lanes in which traffic is permitted in the same direction. When reversible traffic signals are switched off, the driver must immediately move to the right beyond marking 1.9.

Crossing line 1.9 separating opposing traffic flows is prohibited when reversible traffic signals are switched off.

Horizontal marking.title: No parking
Horizontal marking.description: Marks places where parking is prohibited.

Horizontal marking.title: Solid and broken lines
Horizontal marking.description:
Separates traffic flows in opposite or the same directions on road sections where lane changes are permitted from one lane only; marks places where movement must be permitted only from the broken-line side, such as U-turn locations and entrances to or exits from adjoining areas.

Line 1.11 may be crossed from the broken-line side, and also from the solid-line side, but only when completing an overtaking manoeuvre or passing an obstruction.

Horizontal marking.title: Stop line
Horizontal marking.description: Indicates where a driver must stop when sign 2.5 is present or when a traffic signal or traffic controller prohibits movement.

Horizontal marking.title: Give-way line
Horizontal marking.description: Indicates where a driver must stop if necessary to give way to vehicles travelling on the intersecting road.

Horizontal marking.title: Pedestrian crossing
Horizontal marking.description: Marks a pedestrian crossing; the arrows of marking 1.14.2 indicate the direction of pedestrian movement.

Horizontal marking.title: Pedestrian crossing with arrows
Horizontal marking.description: Marks a pedestrian crossing; the arrows of marking 1.14.2 indicate the direction of pedestrian movement.

Horizontal marking.title: Diagonal pedestrian crossing
Horizontal marking.description: Marks a diagonal pedestrian crossing.

Horizontal marking.title: Cycle track crossing
Horizontal marking.description: Marks where a cycle track crosses the carriageway.

Horizontal marking.title: Island separating opposing traffic flows
Horizontal marking.description: Marks islands separating either opposing traffic flows or vehicle parking spaces from cycle lanes.

Horizontal marking.title: Island separating traffic in the same direction
Horizontal marking.description: Marks islands separating traffic flows travelling in the same direction.

Horizontal marking.title: Traffic merging island
Horizontal marking.description: Marks islands where traffic flows merge.

Horizontal marking.title: Route vehicle stop and taxi rank
Horizontal marking.description: Marks stopping places for route vehicles and parking places for vehicles used as passenger taxis.

Horizontal marking.title: Tram stop
Horizontal marking.description: Marks tram stopping places where passengers board or alight from the carriageway or from a boarding island situated on it.

Horizontal marking.title: Directions of movement by lane
Horizontal marking.description: Indicates permitted directions of movement by lane at a junction. A marking with a dead-end symbol indicates that turning onto the nearest carriageway is prohibited; a marking permitting a left turn from the leftmost lane also permits a U-turn.

Horizontal marking.title: Approach to narrowing or a solid line
Horizontal marking.description: Warns of an approach to a narrowing of the carriageway, where the number of lanes in the direction of travel is reduced, or to marking 1.1 or 1.11 separating opposing traffic flows.

Horizontal marking.title: Approach to the give-way line
Horizontal marking.description: Warns of an approach to marking 1.13.

Horizontal marking.title: Approach to the stop line
Horizontal marking.description: Warns of an approach to marking 1.12 where it is used in combination with sign 2.5.

Horizontal marking.title: Road number
Horizontal marking.description: Indicates the road number.

Horizontal marking.title: Lane for route vehicles
Horizontal marking.description: Indicates a dedicated lane for route vehicles.

Horizontal marking.title: Pedestrian path
Horizontal marking.description: Indicates a pedestrian path or the pedestrian part of a path intended for shared movement by pedestrians, persons using personal mobility devices and cyclists.

Horizontal marking.title: Cycle track or lane
Horizontal marking.description: Indicates a cycle track, part of a track, or a cycle lane.

Horizontal marking.title: Repetition of warning signs
Horizontal marking.description: Repeats warning road signs.

Horizontal marking.title: Repetition of prohibitory signs
Horizontal marking.description: Repeats prohibitory road signs.

Horizontal marking.title: Space for vehicles displaying the Disabled sign
Horizontal marking.description: Repeats the Disabled road sign.

Horizontal marking.title: Photo and video enforcement
Horizontal marking.description: Repeats the Photo and video enforcement road sign and/or marks road sections where photo and video enforcement may be carried out; marking 1.24.4 may be used independently.

Horizontal marking.title: Space for electric vehicles
Horizontal marking.description: Repeats plate 8.4.3.1; marking 1.24.5 may be used independently.

Horizontal marking.title: Cycle zone
Horizontal marking.description: Repeats road sign 5.33.1, Cycle zone.

Horizontal marking.title: Parking for diplomatic vehicles
Horizontal marking.description: Repeats road sign 8.9.3, Parking for diplomatic vehicles only.

Horizontal marking.title: Speed hump
Horizontal marking.description: Indicates artificial road humps in accordance with GOST R 52605-2006.

Horizontal marking.title: Junction area
Horizontal marking.description: Marks an area of a junction that must not be entered if a queue ahead would force the driver to stop and obstruct vehicles travelling in the transverse direction, except for right or left turns in cases permitted by the Rules. The marking may be used independently or together with road sign 1.35.

Vertical marking.title: Dangerous structure element: rightward slope
Vertical marking.description: Marks elements of road structures, such as bridge supports, overpasses and end sections of parapets, where these elements pose a danger to moving vehicles.

Vertical marking.title: Dangerous structure element: chevrons
Vertical marking.description: Marks elements of road structures, such as bridge supports, overpasses and end sections of parapets, where these elements pose a danger to moving vehicles.

Vertical marking.title: Dangerous structure element: leftward slope
Vertical marking.description: Marks elements of road structures, such as bridge supports, overpasses and end sections of parapets, where these elements pose a danger to moving vehicles.

Vertical marking.title: Lower edge of a structure
Vertical marking.description: Marks the lower edge of the span of a tunnel, bridge or overpass.

Vertical marking.title: Round bollard
Vertical marking.description: Marks round bollards installed on central reservations or traffic islands.

Vertical marking.title: Guide post
Vertical marking.description: Marks guide posts, bollards, barrier supports and similar objects.

Vertical marking.title: Barrier on a dangerous section
Vertical marking.description: Marks the side surfaces of road barriers on tight bends, steep descents and other dangerous sections.

Vertical marking.title: Barrier on other sections
Vertical marking.description: Marks the side surfaces of road barriers on other sections.

Vertical marking.title: Kerb or traffic island
Vertical marking.description: Marks kerbs on dangerous sections and raised traffic islands.
